exposure: the most common pathogenic mutation m.3243A>G
cohort: 67 women with genetically confirmed mitochondrial disease and 69 unaffected women from the UK Mitochondrial Diseases Cohort
finding: Women with the m.3243A>G mutation experienced significantly more gestational diabetes, breathing difficulties, hypertension, preterm births, emergency caesarean sections, and neonatal complications compared to unaffected women and those with other mitochondrial disease mutations.
mod_finding: Only half of the pregnancies in the m.3243A>G group had normal vaginal delivery, with emergency caesarean section accounting for 24.2% of deliveries.
